authority_note: This checkpoint does not modify companies/SNOW/latest.json or current registry authority. Current canonical authority remains the 2026-09-06 preliminary review until a separate canonical harness run promotes it.
review_method: User-supplied FY2026 10-K, Q2 FY2027 10-Q, Q2 earnings 8-K/Exhibit 99.1, proxy supplement and two Form 144 notices were structured and cross-checked as a non-current research checkpoint.
portfolio_context: No synchronized current quote, tax basis, position size, or portfolio risk budget was supplied. This is not a buy approval or automatic portfolio action.
structural_thesis: Snowflake is showing accelerating product consumption and enterprise AI adoption while retaining strong large-customer expansion metrics. The central investment question is whether this growth converts into durable per-share owner cash after very high stock compensation, equity-tax cash outflows, cloud/AI infrastructure costs and acquisition-related share issuance.
customer_and_moat: Q2 FY2027 product revenue grew about 37%, NRR was 126%, customers above $1M TTM product revenue reached 828, RPO was $9.0B and the company added 692 net new customers. These support a strong customer-value and platform-expansion thesis, but competitive share and independent workload-retention evidence remain incomplete.
current_finding: Operational growth accelerated and management raised FY2027 product-revenue guidance to 36%. However, SBC remains economically dominant: FY2026 SBC exceeded company-defined FCF and H1 FY2027 FCF less SBC remained negative. Share count continued to rise despite repurchases.
economic_finding: The company produces substantial reported FCF, but its FCF definition excludes financing cash outflows for taxes paid on net share settlement. H1 FY2027 FCF of $316.6M was almost fully consumed by $327.7M of those cash outflows before considering the separate $826.1M SBC expense or dilution.
capital_and_survival: Liquidity is strong: July 2026 cash plus short- and long-term investments was about $4.33B against about $2.28B net convertible notes. Near-term survival is not the issue; owner economics, dilution and AI infrastructure returns are.
next_evidence: Synchronized price and 9% reverse DCF; gross and net share dilution bridge; SBC by cohort and repurchase economics; AI workload gross margin and cloud-commitment utilization; independent competitive share/retention evidence; acquisition cash ROIC for Observe and Natoma.
permanent_loss_case: Revenue and AI usage can continue growing while shareholders still suffer if SBC and acquisition shares dilute per-share value, AI/cloud cost intensity prevents durable margin conversion, or the market price already requires sustained high-thirties growth and strong margin expansion.
falsifiers: NRR falls materially below the current mid-120s while product-revenue growth decelerates and RPO/customer expansion weaken together.
SBC plus equity-related cash outflows remain at a level that prevents durable growth in owner cash per share despite revenue growth.
AI inference/GPU cost intensity rises without corresponding product gross-margin or consumption monetization improvement.
Observe/Natoma and future acquisitions consume cash and shares without measurable incremental product revenue, retention, or cash returns above the 9% hurdle.
increase_evidence: SBC as a percent of revenue continues falling and net share count stabilizes or declines without value-destructive repurchases.
Product revenue, NRR and large-customer cohorts remain strong while GAAP operating loss narrows and owner-cash-per-share grows.
AI product adoption converts into measurable incremental consumption and stable/improving product gross margin.
Reverse DCF shows the current price requires assumptions below a defensible Base case.
sell_evidence: Persistent 4%+ annualized gross/net dilution with no offsetting acceleration in owner cash per share.
Material deterioration in enterprise retention or consumption with simultaneous competitive share loss.
AI/cloud commitments or acquisitions produce structurally lower incremental returns while the valuation remains demanding.
